source.title: Tonic dopamine: opportunity costs and the control of response vigor

confidence_rationale: Canonical normative RL theory establishing vigour as a separable control quantity (tonic DA / opportunity cost) distinct from phasic action-selection -- conceptually close to REE's substrate. But it is a model, not a measurement of separable learnable channels, and is silent on the improves-conversion question; it also argues one scalar suffices for vigour.
failure_signatures: The model collapses vigour into a single global scalar (average reward rate), so it actually supports COMPRESSION at the vigour level -- one scalar is normatively optimal, in mild tension with MECH-451 expecting vigour to need fine sub-channels.
Vigour-as-opportunity-cost is a global quantity, not state-specific, so it does not by itself support different control functions mattering in different states.

mapping.source_claim_statement: The long-run average reward rate sets optimal response vigour as an opportunity cost and is plausibly reported by TONIC dopamine, computationally separate from the PHASIC dopamine signal driving discrete action selection.
mapping.ree_translation: Grounds the 'vigour/dopaminergic' finer channel of MECH-451 as a separable control dimension with a different computational role (sets response rate) than the motor-value channel that selects among actions.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Normative model, not a behaving-brain measurement of segregated learnable channels; supports that vigour is a distinct controllable quantity but NOT that adding a separate vigour channel to a gating layer improves committed-action conversion.
mapping.source_context: Average-reward reinforcement-learning theory of response latency/vigour.

confidence_components.notes: Low transfer risk conceptually (it is itself an RL formalism close to REE) but the improves-conversion claim is out of scope.
